name: Neck strengthening
pattern: The head moves (or holds) against resistance: nodding down (flexion), tipping back (extension), ear to shoulder (side bend), plus chin tucks for the deep neck flexors.
setup: Sit tall with your back supported, or lie on a bench with your head just off the end.
Shoulders down and still; only the head moves.
Start with your hand or a light band as resistance.

steps.text: Move the head slowly through a comfortable range: chin down, head back, or ear toward shoulder.
Pause briefly at the end of the range.

cues.cue: Lead with a small chin tuck, like a nod.
cues.why: The deep neck flexors control the head nod; they are often weak and late in people with neck pain.

cues.cue: Shoulders stay still; only the head moves.
cues.why: Shrugging hands the work to the upper traps.
Progressive neck training reduced pain and disability in women with chronic neck pain.

cues.cue: Smooth, pain-free range; no fast jerks.
cues.why: Head-harness training increased neck strength and muscle size when done in a controlled range.

breathing: Breathe out as you push, in as you return. Don't hold your breath.

tempo.note: Move in about 2 s, return in 3. Isometric holds 5-10 s.

mistakes.name: Chin pokes forward
mistakes.looks: The chin juts forward instead of nodding.
mistakes.fix: Tuck the chin first, then move.
mistakes.why: The upper neck extends and the deep flexors switch off.

mistakes.name: Shrugging
mistakes.fix: Shoulders down and back; lighter load.

mistakes.name: Jerky, end-range swings
mistakes.looks: The head flings into full extension or flexion.
mistakes.fix: Slow down and stop short of the end.
mistakes.why: Fast end-range loading strains the neck.

safety: Arm pain, tingling, numbness, dizziness or headache with neck movement: stop and see a clinician.
After a neck injury, get cleared before loaded neck work.
Neck stretches belong to stretching; this family is for strength and control.

variants.change: External load (plate, harness, cable, machine): for athletes and strength goals.
Hold still against your hand or a band: safest way to start.
Lying: gravity is the load; face down trains extensors, face up trains flexors.
Rotation: turn the head side to side against resistance.

subtypes.name: Chin tuck
subtypes.change: Glide the head straight back and nod slightly, making a double chin; hold, then relax.

subtypes.name: Lying neck flexion
subtypes.change: On your back, head off the bench end; curl the chin toward the chest.

subtypes.name: Lying or prone neck extension
subtypes.change: Face down, head off the bench end; lift the head back until level or slightly higher.

subtypes.name: Neck side flexion
subtypes.change: Ear toward shoulder against a band, harness or hand; the convention has no neck side-bend key, so the rig needs one (about 30-40 degrees, estimate).

motion.basis: Default is seated flexion then extension. Working range kept short of normal end range (about 50 flexion and 60-70 extension in healthy adults, swinkels2014, approximate). Side flexion and rotation have no convention key. Angles estimated.
